title: The Unsaid Interior
premise: After her father's funeral, Isandro Underhill returns to the shuttered family house in Marrow Bay to catalog what was never said—letters, ledgers, and a locked room her mother kept for forty years. A stranger named Wren Corliss appears claiming the family once lived under another name, Halloway, and that Isandro's father was not the man who raised her. Sorting truth from loyalty, Isandro uncovers that her parents sheltered a fugitive identity after a fire that killed another family, and that the 'stranger' is the daughter of those who died. In the end, Isandro chooses truth over inherited silence: she opens the locked room, publishes the family's confession, and lets Wren into the fragile found family that remains—grief transmuted into reckoning rather than erasure.
about_author: Isandro Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the unopened letters of estranged families. Their fiction excavates the quiet violence of polite households, and they write from a coastal town they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV at the funeral, performing flawless grief while deflecting every mourner. A woman in a gray coat watches her too long. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being seen without being known.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Still Isandro's POV. The stranger, Wren, says the word 'Halloway' and Isandro's rehearsed composure cracks for the first time. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground of her identity shifting.

chapters.title: Inventory of Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro begins cataloging the house: labeled boxes, unsent letters, a ledger of payments to an unknown 'M.C.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as methodical calm.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She finds the door her mother kept locked for forty years; her father's will mentions it obliquely. Emotional beat: the pull of forbidden knowledge versus trained obedience.

chapters.title: Wren Corliss
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, first appearance. She explains she grew up on stories of Marrow Bay and a family that 'borrowed' her parents' name. Emotional beat: her hunger for answers she's chased since childhood.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Isandro traces payments to a burned-out property outside town and to a retired constable. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Constable's Memory
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The dying constable, Aldous Meek, half-confirms: there was a fire in 1983, two families, and a bargain. Emotional beat: history pressing its thumb on the present.

chapters.title: Halloway House Burns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, recounting her mother's fragmented memories of the fire that killed her grandparents. Emotional beat: inherited grief meeting Isandro's inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Left
chapters.summary: Isandro confronts her estranged aunt, Vivian, who fled the family decades ago. Vivian says only: 'Ask about the other child.' Emotional beat: the family's silence has enforcers, not just victims.

chapters.title: The Other Child
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Records suggest her father had a sibling who died in the fire—the fire her parents may have survived by switching identities. Emotional beat: mourning a father who was never real.

chapters.title: Marrow Bay, Out of Season
chapters.summary: Wren and Isandro, forced together, walk the burned property. They find a child's tin box buried in ash soil. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, first shared laughter.

chapters.title: The Tin Box
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Inside: photographs of two families side by side, and her mother's handwriting naming the dead as 'the price.' Emotional beat: horror at her mother's cold accounting.

chapters.title: Vivian Returns
chapters.summary: Aunt Vivian arrives uninvited, demanding the house be sold and the past sealed. She and Wren clash. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized—Vivian claims silence is love.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, night scene. She picks the lock of the locked room and finds her mother's confession, unwritten: blank paper, forty years of it. Emotional beat: the devastating discovery that silence was a choice renewed daily.

chapters.title: The Price of the Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She admits she came not for truth but for the house—her family's stolen inheritance. Isandro overhears. Emotional beat: the fragile alliance fractures.

chapters.title: Auction of Ashes
chapters.summary: Vivian moves to sell the house; a developer with his own interest in the Halloway land emerges as the story's antagonist. Emotional beat: the past is profitable to those without consciences.

chapters.title: The Confession Isandro Writes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She drafts the family's true history to block the sale and free the house's story. Emotional beat: choosing truth over the family's survival-by-silence.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Door
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Vivian, the developer, and Wren converge as Isandro reads the confession aloud in the locked room. Emotional beat: the unsaid finally spoken, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Fire, Remembered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The full account of 1983: her grandparents died because Isandro's father chose escape over warning. Emotional beat: rage and grief without a villain to punish.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: The developer forces an emergency sale; Isandro must decide in hours whether to sign away the truth with the house. Emotional beat: the last test of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: The Room Opens
chapters.summary: Climax. Isandro refuses to sign, deeding the house and land to Wren and a memorial trust, publicly ending the Halloway silence. Vivian walks out; the family, as it was, is over. Emotional beat: ruin as liberation.

chapters.title: What We Say Now
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. A year later, Isandro and Wren catalog the house together—this time writing things down. A new, chosen family forms around told truth. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
